title: The 8 Levels of Relief
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis called Orchard City, where fruit and vegetable people commute on crowded subway lines, grab overpriced coffee at corner kiosks, and stress over rent, rent hikes, and social obligations.
catchphrase: The number on the forehead never lies.
links: Level 1 mentions a quiet regular named Mr. Chestnut who always leaves a massive tip at the subway kiosk.
Level 2's barista drops a cup meant for the ambitious Dragonfruit executive from Level 7.
Level 3's canceled dinner was supposed to be hosted at the luxury rooftop apartment of Level 8.
Level 4's missed dentist appointment frees up a slot taken by the Lemon from Level 6.
Level 5 overhears the Coconut from Level 8 complaining about his overly packed social calendar in the elevator.
Level 6 finds a dropped gold coin near the subway turnstile left by the nervous Broccoli from Level 1.
Level 7's cancelled board meeting saves her from running into her estranged cousin, the Lemon from Level 6.
Level 8 resolves the mystery of the missing gold coins and reveals why everyone's number shifted that stormy Tuesday.

levels.name: Broccoli Ben, 24, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 1. Level 1: 0% relief when your phone buzzes with a birthday invite you cannot afford. I stared at my cracked phone screen in the damp subway car while my neon badge flashed a miserable 0 percent relief. My rent is $1,450 for a tiny closet, and my bank account holds exactly $12.43. Then my phone buzzed with the group chat notification. Tonight at 8 PM, mandatory upscale dinner at the steakhouse. I buried my face in my hands, calculating how many instant ramen packs I would need to survive the month if I went. Stop whining, Ben, just show up and smile. I looked up and saw a sharply dressed Orange glaring down at my forehead display. You are ruining the aesthetic of our table with that pathetic zero. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Lemon Lily, 29, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 2. Level 2: 15% relief when you see the group chat message: Dinner is canceled. I was wiping down the sticky counter at the neon-lit corner cafe, my forehead badge glowing a stressful 15 percent relief. My feet throbbed after standing for nine hours straight, earning minimum wage plus meager tips. My roommate had just texted insisting I attend her ridiculous birthday dinner tonight at a pricey bistro. I didn't have the $80 for my share, nor the emotional energy to fake a smile. Then my phone lit up on the counter. Dinner is officially canceled due to food poisoning. Your little happy dance is holding up my custom oat milk order, you absolute failure. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Strawberry Sam, 32, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 3. Level 3: 30% relief when the team meeting is postponed an hour before sign-off. I rubbed my stinging eyes under the harsh fluorescent lights of the cubicle farm, my forehead badge stubbornly reading 30 percent relief. Piles of tax spreadsheets towered over my desk while my inbox screamed with 412 unread emails. My boss had scheduled a mandatory Friday evening strategy sync at a downtown hotel, and I was dreading every second of it. Suddenly, a company-wide email popped up: Tonight's strategy sync is canceled due to a plumbing emergency on the 8th floor. I let out a gasp so loud my neighbor dropped his stapler. Pure, sweet freedom. We still have three quarterly audits to finish before you even think about breathing. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Orange Olivia, 35, Realtor
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 4. Level 4: 45% relief when the home inspection is called off because of a storm. I stood in the pouring rain outside a $750,000 suburban fixer-upper, my forehead badge glowing a steady 45 percent relief. My commission check from last month had barely covered my BMW lease, and my schedule was packed tighter than a subway car. The buyers had demanded a thorough foundation inspection this afternoon, threatening to back out of the deal entirely. Then my phone rang with a call from the inspector. Lightning struck the transformer on the block, inspection's off until Tuesday. I let out a triumphant laugh that scared a nearby pigeon. No awkward small talk with picky clients today. Watch where you are parking, cheapskate. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Avocado Adam, 41, Consultant
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 5. Level 5: 55% relief when your high-society charity gala gets postponed. I adjusted my silk tie in the lobby mirror of my luxury apartment building, my forehead badge glowing a confident 55 percent relief. My consulting fees are $250 an hour, but my social calendar is an absolute nightmare of pretentious events I loathe attending. Tonight's charity ball for antique teacups was slated to be three hours of forced small talk with wealthy snobs. Then my concierge handed me a gold-embossed letter. Gala postponed due to a catering kitchen fire. I smiled so wide my cheeks hurt. Total, unadulterated freedom for a Friday night. Watch where you are stepping, suit-wearing clown. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Lemon Laura, 46, Art Gallery Owner
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 6. Level 6: 70% relief when the VIP vernissage is canceled because the main artist caught the flu. I stood in the center of my upscale art gallery surrounded by overpriced abstract canvases, my forehead badge glowing a sharp 70 percent relief. My rent for this prime downtown space is $9,000 a month, and the pressure to impress wealthy investors is suffocating. Tonight's grand opening was supposed to feature champagne, pretentious critics, and four hours of fake laughter. Then my phone chimed with a message from the artist. Severe laryngitis, opening postponed until next month. I let out a loud cackle that echoed off the white brick walls. Sweet, glorious solitude. Stop laughing like a witch, gallery owner. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Dragonfruit Diana, 52, CEO
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 7. Level 7: 85% relief when the board meeting gets called off due to a city-wide blackout. I stood in my penthouse corner office overlooking the glowing skyline of Orchard City, my forehead badge flashing an impressive 85 percent relief. My corporate empire generates millions, but endless board meetings and investor dinners drain my soul. Tonight's annual gala dinner with the city council was scheduled to be a five-hour endurance test of fake smiles and political backstabbing. Then the power grid failed, plunging the downtown core into darkness. Emergency blackout, gala canceled until further notice, my assistant announced over the intercom. Not so fast, Diana. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Coconut Carl, 60, Billionaire Investor
levels.story: The 8 levels of relief when plans get canceled. Level 8. Level 8: 100% relief when you cancel every meeting on Earth and buy a one-way ticket to nowhere. I sat in my private garden overlooking the entire glittering metropolis of Orchard City, my forehead badge glowing a blinding, permanent 100 percent relief. People always assume having millions means you never have to deal with annoying social obligations, but the truth is, everyone's hiding behind their numbers. All those angry baristas, stressed accountants, and arrogant executives I crossed paths with—they were all just craving the exact same thing: permission to stay home. My phone buzzed one last time with a notification that every single gala, dinner, and board meeting in the city had been permanently canceled. I tossed my phone into the fountain, took a sip of fresh coconut water, and smiled. Which number represents your life right now, and what series should we explore next?
